requirements.evidence:
The code cannot run: app/Models/EntityInvite.php:6 imports HasFactory from a namespace that doesn't exist, `Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Attributes\HasFactory`. app/Livewire/Entity/Members.php:72 has a PHP syntax error, `catch (\\Illuminate\\Database\\QueryException $e)`. Members has no openMember/saveRole/confirmRemoval/cancelRemoval and none of the selectedMembershipId/memberRole/confirmingRemoval properties. assignRole is kept (Members.php:101), there is no manager-only mount and no rate limit. PendingInvites::accept leaves `// TODO: set tenant session and redirect` (PendingInvites.php:23). The pending-invites view is the placeholder `
Pending Invites List
` and is not added to the switcher or onboarding. The mailable has no ShouldQueue and no content(), and the 'Access the link below...' line and the lang/pt_BR.json entries are missing.

conventions.evidence: No app/Actions class for sending, accepting or declining invites; the writes are inline in the components (Members.php:65, PendingInvites.php:23-28). Authorization in PendingInvites uses a hand-rolled abort_if email check instead of a policy. The migration file name 2026_10_29_000000 looks hand-written. Factory has no namespace. No docs or CHANGELOG updates. No tests.

security.evidence: sendInvite has no RateLimiter, although the task requires one. mount() is still not restricted to managers, and assignRole is still public (Members.php:101). accept() creates a membership without checking for an existing one and without a transaction (PendingInvites.php:23-28). $fillable is `[]` while a #[Fillable] attribute sits on the property (EntityInvite.php:21-29), so mass assignment is effectively broken or unclear. On the plus side, sendInvite and cancelInvite call authorize('update') and cancelInvite resolves the invite through $this->entity->invites().

tests.evidence: The diff contains no test files at all. There are no happy-path, validation, unauthorized-call or tamper tests for sendInvite, cancelInvite, accept or decline.

simplicity.evidence: The code is fairly direct, but the two existence checks repeat the same error (Members.php:51-61). Catching QueryException by code 23000 (Members.php:72-77) is more fragile than catching UniqueConstraintViolationException. The factory adds a forEntity() state instead of defaulting to Entity::factory().

readability.evidence: There is a dead comment `// removed addMember method` (Members.php:99), a TODO left in place of the required behaviour (PendingInvites.php:33), and unused imports (BelongsToMany in EntityInvite.php:9, BelongsTo in EntityInviteFactory.php:5). The use statements in Members.php:9-11 are out of order, `fn($q)=>$q->where('email',$email)` is unformatted, and `reset(['email', ...])` refers to a property that no longer exists.

scope.evidence: Every file in the diff relates to the invite feature. The only extras are a small one: the unrequested factory state forEntity() and the invitedBy() relation.

issues.explanation: `catch (\\Illuminate\\Database\\QueryException $e)` uses double backslashes, which is a PHP parse error, so the component cannot load.
HasFactory is imported from `Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Attributes`, which doesn't exist. The trait lives in `Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Factories`, so the model fails to load.

A #[Fillable] attribute is applied to a property declared `$fillable = []`. The model ends up with no fillable attributes, so EntityInvite::create() will throw MassAssignmentException or silently drop fields.

None of the members-page redesign is implemented: no manager-only mount or route, no openMember/saveRole/confirmRemoval/cancelRemoval, none of the required properties, no view changes, and assignRole is still present.
The change ships no tests, although the conventions require every feature to have tests, including unauthorized-call and tamper tests.
accept() leaves a TODO instead of setting the tenant session and redirecting. It also creates the membership without guarding against duplicates and without a transaction.
The view is a placeholder with no list and no Accept/Decline buttons, and it is not included on the entity switcher or onboarding (no hr/title handling).
sendInvite() has no rate limit, although the task requires 10 successful invites per manager and entity per hour.

The pending-invite check ignores expires_at, so an expired invite blocks a new one instead of being replaced. Even if the check passed, the expired row is never deleted, so the insert would hit the unique constraint.
The mailable does not implement ShouldQueue, defines build() instead of content() (breaking the `content()->markdown` contract) and doesn't set the PegaFila theme.
The 'Access the link below to sign in and accept your invite:' line is missing. Strings live in lang/*/emails.php instead of the required lang/pt_BR.json translation keys.
E-mail is not normalized in the model, which the task requires so every write path agrees. Only sendInvite lowercases the address.
Domain writes (create invite, accept, decline) are not in app/Actions classes, and authorization uses abort_if instead of policies.
`$this->reset(['email','inviteRole'])` resets a removed property and never clears inviteEmail.
The error keys entity.invite_exists and entity.invite_expired are used, but their translations are not added in the diff.
The factory has no namespace and defaults entity_id to null, while the contract says the default is an entity.
The migration appears hand-written rather than generated, and its enum allows 'owner', which is never invitable.
There are no updates to the docs (business rules, database schema) or to the CHANGELOG.
The dead comment `// removed addMember method`, unused imports and unformatted closures would fail Pint and add noise.

review.summary: The change starts the invite feature: model, migration, factory, mailable, a partial sendInvite/cancelInvite and a stub PendingInvites component. It contains fatal errors (a PHP syntax error in the catch clause, a wrong HasFactory import, a broken $fillable). Most requirements are missing: the members-page modals and role/removal flow, manager-only access, rate limiting, the accept redirect and the pending-invites UI. There are no tests, so the change should be rejected.
